input.findings:
Author/parent provisional analysis (for expert validation — challenge freely):

P0/P1 candidate — Independent releasability / old-provider regression: client.py now raises RuntimeError("Provider did not acknowledge applied settings") whenever response.get("applied") is not True. The currently supported provider returns {"ok": True} with no "applied" key (HEAD test mock evidences this; Task 2 provider receipts are pending in a separate repo). So if this client increment ships to main independently (an explicit spec requirement), EVERY ordinary save against the supported provider raises -> ordinary saves stop working at eval-release. This appears to directly violate design.md: "Ordinary saves must continue to work with the supported provider at eval-release" AND "preserving independently releasable main." This is an in-scope regression in Task 1, not a complaint that Task 2 is missing.

Contributing factor — ungated enforcement: enhanced_settings defaults to False ("enhanced UI disabled by default"), yet both the "require_receipt": True request field and the strict applied-check are applied unconditionally, independent of the flag. A natural fix is to gate the receipt requirement behind enhanced_settings (or a provider-capability negotiation), so the default/ordinary path keeps its old behavior until the provider supports receipts.

Test-coverage concern: tests/test_client.py was edited so the mock send returns {"ok": True, "applied": True}, i.e. the mock was upgraded to the not-yet-deployed provider behavior. The green test therefore does NOT exercise the supported-provider (no "applied") path, masking the regression. No test covers old-provider compatibility.

Minor/quality: `response.get("applied") is not True` is intentionally strict (rejects truthy-but-not-True); confirm that's desired. Overall error handling is reasonable (raises on failure). No security issues spotted in the diff itself.

Baseline note: provider repo is a separate repo, not available locally; exact deployed provider behavior is Unknown and is the key piece of missing evidence. The conclusion rests on the HEAD test mock + the pending/separate status of Task 2.

issues_found.description: Client unconditionally requires response['applied'] is True; supported provider does not return 'applied', so independent release to main breaks all ordinary saves — violates design.md delivery contract.
Receipt enforcement not gated by enhanced_settings flag (default disabled) nor by capability negotiation; applied to default ordinary path.
Unit test mock upgraded to not-yet-deployed provider behavior ({'applied': True}); masks the old-provider regression, no coverage of supported-provider path.
